headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.//: Vite stamps a content hash into every asset filename, so a changed file is a changed URL and this can never serve stale code. Listed after the catch-all so this Cache-Control wins.
The HTML shell is the opposite case: it names the current asset hashes, so it must be revalidated on every visit or a deploy would never be picked up.
